bandwidth utilization: The wise use of available bandwidth; two categories: multiplexing (goal efficiency) and spectrum spreading (goal privacy, not covered). See [Bandwidth utilization and multiplexing](#/comp3721-w6/multiplexing).
multiplexing: The set of techniques that allow the simultaneous transmission of multiple signals across a single data link; combining several channels into one. See [Bandwidth utilization and multiplexing](#/comp3721-w6/multiplexing).
spectrum spreading: The other bandwidth-utilization category; goal privacy; not discussed in this class. See [Bandwidth utilization and multiplexing](#/comp3721-w6/multiplexing).
MUX|multiplexer: The device that combines n input lines onto one link. See [Bandwidth utilization and multiplexing](#/comp3721-w6/multiplexing).
DEMUX|demultiplexer: The device that separates the one link back into n output lines. See [Bandwidth utilization and multiplexing](#/comp3721-w6/multiplexing).
link (multiplexing): Link refers to the physical path. See [Bandwidth utilization and multiplexing](#/comp3721-w6/multiplexing).
channel: Channel refers to the portion of a link; one link, n channels. See [Bandwidth utilization and multiplexing](#/comp3721-w6/multiplexing).
FDM|frequency-division multiplexing: An analog multiplexing technique: the signals modulate different carrier frequencies and are combined into a single composite signal; used when the link's bandwidth (in hertz) is greater than the combined bandwidths of the signals. See [FDM: carriers, guard bands and the 20 to 32 kHz example](#/comp3721-w6/fdm).
guard band|guard bands: Strips of unused bandwidth that separate channels from each other, to prevent signals from overlapping and interference; n channels need n − 1 guard bands. See [FDM: carriers, guard bands and the 20 to 32 kHz example](#/comp3721-w6/fdm).
composite signal (FDM): The sum of the modulated signals carried by the link. See [FDM: carriers, guard bands and the 20 to 32 kHz example](#/comp3721-w6/fdm).
WDM|wavelength-division multiplexing: An analog multiplexing technique to combine optical signals on a fibre-optic cable; like FDM but with very high frequencies; combining and splitting handled by a prism. See [WDM: FDM for light](#/comp3721-w6/wdm).
prism: Combines and splits the light sources in WDM. See [WDM: FDM for light](#/comp3721-w6/wdm).
TDM|time-division multiplexing: A digital multiplexing technique that allows several digital signals to share the high bandwidth of a link in time; combines several low-rate channels into a high-rate one. See [Synchronous TDM: units, slots, frames and rates](#/comp3721-w6/synchronous-tdm).
synchronous TDM: Each input's units take turns in fixed slots; the output link's data rate is n times the data rate of a connection; the unit duration is n times shorter. See [Synchronous TDM: units, slots, frames and rates](#/comp3721-w6/synchronous-tdm).
unit: The piece of an input connection's data flow placed in one slot; 1 bit, one character, or one block of data. See [Synchronous TDM: units, slots, frames and rates](#/comp3721-w6/synchronous-tdm).
frame (TDM): A round of data units from each input connection; n slots for n connections; its duration is the duration of an input unit T. See [Synchronous TDM: units, slots, frames and rates](#/comp3721-w6/synchronous-tdm).
time slot|slot: One unit's place in a frame; duration T/n. See [Synchronous TDM: units, slots, frames and rates](#/comp3721-w6/synchronous-tdm).
frame rate: The number of frames per second; always the same as any input unit rate (Example 2: 100 kbps ÷ 2 bits = 50 000 frames/s). See [Synchronous TDM: units, slots, frames and rates](#/comp3721-w6/synchronous-tdm).
statistical TDM: Improves efficiency by removing the empty slots from the frame (named only). See [Empty slots, data-rate management and framing bits](#/comp3721-w6/tdm-rate-management).
empty slot: The slot of a source with no data to send; why synchronous TDM is not efficient. See [Empty slots, data-rate management and framing bits](#/comp3721-w6/tdm-rate-management).
multilevel multiplexing: Used when the data rate of an input line is a multiple of others; lower-rate lines are multiplexed first (20 + 20 → 40 kbps, then 4 × 40 → 160 kbps). See [Empty slots, data-rate management and framing bits](#/comp3721-w6/tdm-rate-management).
multiple-slot allocation: Allocating more than one slot in a frame to a single input line when it has multiple rates of the others (50 kbps gets two 25 kbps slots; 125 kbps out). See [Empty slots, data-rate management and framing bits](#/comp3721-w6/tdm-rate-management).
pulse stuffing|bit padding|bit stuffing: Used when the bit rates of sources are not integer multiples of each other; the highest input rate becomes the dominant data rate and dummy bits are added to the slower lines (46 → 50 kbps; 150 kbps out). See [Empty slots, data-rate management and framing bits](#/comp3721-w6/tdm-rate-management).
framing bits|synchronization bits: One or more bits usually added to the beginning of each frame, following a pattern (1 0 1 …) frame to frame so the demultiplexer can separate the time slots accurately. See [Empty slots, data-rate management and framing bits](#/comp3721-w6/tdm-rate-management).
node: A host or a router; the data-link layer moves a frame from one node to the next. See [Node-to-node communication, framing and the four services](#/comp3721-w6/data-link-services).
link: The connection between two nodes (a LAN or a point-to-point network). See [Node-to-node communication, framing and the four services](#/comp3721-w6/data-link-services).
frame: A packet at the data-link layer is called a frame. See [Node-to-node communication, framing and the four services](#/comp3721-w6/data-link-services).
framing: Encapsulating the datagram in a frame before sending it to the next node. See [Node-to-node communication, framing and the four services](#/comp3721-w6/data-link-services).
flow control: Controlling the rate of producing frames with respect to the rate of consumed frames. See [Node-to-node communication, framing and the four services](#/comp3721-w6/data-link-services).
error control: Error detection and correction. See [Node-to-node communication, framing and the four services](#/comp3721-w6/data-link-services).
congestion control: The fourth service on the slide's list. See [Node-to-node communication, framing and the four services](#/comp3721-w6/data-link-services).
DLC|data link control: The sublayer dealing with issues common to both point-to-point (dedicated) and broadcast (shared) links: framing, flow control, error control. See [Node-to-node communication, framing and the four services](#/comp3721-w6/data-link-services).
MAC sublayer|media access control: The sublayer dealing only with issues specific to broadcast (shared) links. See [Node-to-node communication, framing and the four services](#/comp3721-w6/data-link-services).
link-layer address|physical address|MAC: The address in the frame header; link-layer address = physical address = MAC address; in Ethernet 48 bits (6 bytes), 12 hexadecimal digits separated by colons; the two addresses in a frame change every time the frame moves from one link to another. See [Link-layer (MAC) addresses and why they change at every hop](#/comp3721-w6/link-layer-addressing).
OUI|organizationally unique identifier: The first three bytes of a MAC address, identifying the vendor (F0:1F:C7 → Apple). See [Link-layer (MAC) addresses and why they change at every hop](#/comp3721-w6/link-layer-addressing).
layer 2 switch|link-layer switch: Involved only in two layers, data-link and physical; sends data only to the single device it is intended for. See [Link-layer (MAC) addresses and why they change at every hop](#/comp3721-w6/link-layer-addressing).
order of addresses: IP addresses: source-destination. Link-layer addresses: destination-source. See [Link-layer (MAC) addresses and why they change at every hop](#/comp3721-w6/link-layer-addressing).
ARP|Address Resolution Protocol: One of the auxiliary protocols defined in the network layer; maps an IP address to a link-layer address; runs all the time in the background. See [ARP: mapping an IP address to a MAC address](#/comp3721-w6/arp).
ARP request: Broadcast to every node on the link: looking for the link-layer address of the node with IP address N₂; operation 1; destination hardware address empty (all 0s). See [ARP: mapping an IP address to a MAC address](#/comp3721-w6/arp).
ARP reply: Unicast to the requester: I am the node and my link-layer address is L₂; operation 2. See [ARP: mapping an IP address to a MAC address](#/comp3721-w6/arp).
hardware type: The ARP field naming the LAN or WAN protocol; 0x0001 = Ethernet. See [ARP: mapping an IP address to a MAC address](#/comp3721-w6/arp).
protocol type: The ARP field naming the network-layer protocol; 0x0800 = IPv4. See [ARP: mapping an IP address to a MAC address](#/comp3721-w6/arp).
broadcast address|BA: The frame destination of an ARP request. See [ARP: mapping an IP address to a MAC address](#/comp3721-w6/arp).
forwarding table: Gives the next-hop IP address for a destination (N_B → N₁ at Alice, N₃ at R1, N_B at R2). See [Alice's datagram to Bob: the frames at every node](#/comp3721-w6/alice-to-bob).
next hop: The node whose MAC address ARP must find before the frame can be sent. See [Alice's datagram to Bob: the frames at every node](#/comp3721-w6/alice-to-bob).
